title: observability: token-level KV cache cost/latency dashboards + alert tuning
author: Priya Nambiar
description: Context: Recent capacity and cost incidents highlighted gaps in token-level observability for KV cache behavior which made it hard to distinguish higher token cost due to cache-miss amplification vs model-side latency. This PR adds token-level KV cache metrics, a set of Grafana dashboards in the Console, and tuned alerting rules so oncall can reliably detect cost/latency regressions attributable to caching. Motivation: reduce mean time to detect and triage cost spikes tied to KV cache health, and provide per-route and per-model cost-per-token breakdowns so product and infra teams can make informed routing and quantization decisions. Changes: 1) instrumented KV layer to emit prom metrics: redwood_kv_cache_hits_total, redwood_kv_cache_misses_total, redwood_kv_cache_hit_ratio (labelled by route, model, region, tenant), redwood_token_cost_per_token_estimated (route/model/region), and updated span tags for tracing to include kv_hit=true/false. 2) added a Grafana dashboard json dashboards/grafana/token_kv_cost_dashboard.json with panels: token cost heatmap, per-route cost breakdown, kv hit-ratio timeseries, kv miss tail latency, and correlation panels linking token cost to kv-miss events. 3) added Prometheus alerting rules prometheus/alerts/kv_token_cost_rules.yml with tuned thresholds and multi-window aggregations: alert KVTokenCostRegression when cost_per_token increases > 15% over 3h vs 24h baseline with kv_miss_rate > 0.2, alert KVCacheDegradation when kv_hit_ratio < 0.85 for 30m and sustained. 4) Console integrations: wired dashboard into /observability/token-kv section and added runbook links and recommended remediation playbook. 5) tests: unit tests for instrumentation, integration test for metrics emission, and an e2e smoke that validates dashboard panels render. Rollout plan: feature-gated on prod by default true for internal accounts and opt-in for early enterprise customers for 2 weeks while we monitor false positives. If a noisy alert is observed, ops can flip the alert_sensitivity flag in config to lower sensitivity. Backwards compatibility: metrics are additive and default labels match existing conventions. Related: ENG-9145 (observability token-level followup), SUP-3412 (customer reported cost spike). Testing and CI: initial CI run surfaced a flakey integration test around kv metrics emission which was addressed by adding a stricter test harness wait and a follow-up commit that reduces race conditions in the test. All checks passing after re-run. Merge: squash and merge after approvals. Monitoring after merge: we will monitor weekly for alert noise for two weeks and adjust thresholds as needed.
